IAMA Contractor for one of the nation's top oil companies. I work in the Eagle Ford Shale, in South Texas. AMAA!

How do you feel about how alternative energy relates to your industry? Do you feel as though oil as a whole will eventually be downsized as a result of cheaper alternatives? If this happens, do you feel your company would be able to re-train employees/restructure to stay competetive?

I'm honestly pretty pumped about alternative energy. Oil seems to be a super efficient resource, but unfortunately not infinite.

As far as oil companies getting their foot in the door on alternative energy, I think the companies whom will succeed at that are probably the ones who are already doing it. As for the one I work for, I'm not sure if they are or not, but I have a sneaking suspicion that the end of oil will mean the end of this company.

I have a friend who worked on off shore rigs before the BP spill. About 6 months after the spill, he quit saying bosses had turned into assholes, that things had become too strict.

I felt bad for his situation but was glad to hear regulations were being focused on.

Have you had expirences like this or seen anything ecologically worrisome?

Edit: Also, "hi" from San Antonio, fellow Texan. :)

Spills are usually less of a big deal out here, partly because they happen less (I deal with wells that have already been drilled and automated), and party because they usually happen in small quantities, and are easy to clean up. Anything over 5 gallons on the ground is still a big deal though.

That being said, pretty much all of the bosses who work directly for the oil company are ducks, in my experience. The pressure seems to be pretty high on those guys, and they have a lot to juggle.

What are some cool new technology used in the oil industry?

How are the owners of smaller oil companies in real life compared to TV/Movies (cowboy clothing, large car with horns at the front, etc.)

Renewables are coming up but oil is used for a lot more things than energy, so I guess your industry is safe in the short run, but is there any concern about biotech? That gene modified bacteria sooner or later (well much later) will be able to produce most if not all oil derivatives.

Since you are in Texas. Which is the best way to cook a steak? (grill/pan? Rare/medium rare? Any spice?)

The tech out here where I work isn't anything very special, mostly piping, pressure gauges and liquid sensors. What I do think is really neat though, is the way everything out here works together. On a typical well, you have a generator, which powers a pumping unit (horse head). That pumping unit pulls oil, water, natural gas, and whatever else up out of the well, and sends it through the line to the separating equipment. The equipment separates the oil, gas, and water/junk. The oil goes into a rank for storing, as does the water. The natural gas that comes up is used to power ALL of the equipment (it's all pressure operated, not engine operated). Some of that natural gas is also used to power the generator, which is powering the pumping unit, and so on. It's all relatively self sustaining!

As far as steak goes, I'm not much of a cook, so however momma fixes it ;)

I'll keep it simple.

Job title and job description?

Wage?

Hours and schedule?

Technically there are 3 or 4 job titles that I fill at different times, but for most of the time, it's Well Monitor/Pumper. Any time an automated well shuts itself off (there are many possible reasons for this. Usually too much/too little pressure/liquid somewhere), myself, or someone like me, drives out there, figures out what's wrong, fixes it if possible, and then opens the well back up and makes sure it stays fixed.

My pay is $400/day before taxes. With how my schedule works out, I typically expect to make $100-120k per year. That is before taxes.

12 hour shifts, and I'm currently working nights. So typically I'll get to work at 6pm, and leave at 6am. Scheduling is ultimately my choice, but I obviously don't want to be a dick, so I stick around if we're shorthanded, try to take time off when we have extra guys around, etc. I usually like to work for 1.5-2 months straight, and then take 1-3 weeks off. There is the odd day off during the stretch of work days.
